external_entities.name: reader
external_entities.description: A person who accesses the public site and fetches assets from the CDN.
external_entities.source_excerpt: Public site: readers hit the web server over HTTPS

external_entities.name: admin
external_entities.description: A person who maintains the database directly.
external_entities.source_excerpt: There is an admin who maintains the database directly

external_entities.name: CDN
external_entities.description: The CDN from which readers fetch images, stylesheets and downloads.
external_entities.source_excerpt: Readers fetch those from the CDN over HTTP.

processes.name: web server
processes.description: The public-facing server that runs the CMS and receives reader requests.
processes.source_excerpt: The web server runs the CMS

processes.name: CMS
processes.description: The content management system running on the web server.
processes.source_excerpt: The web server runs the CMS

data_stores.name: MySQL database
data_stores.description: The database containing pages, accounts and comments.
data_stores.source_excerpt: keeps pages, accounts and comments in a MySQL database
data_stores.notes: The source does not say whether the database is encrypted on disk.

data_stores.name: CDN bucket
data_stores.description: The CDN bucket to which the web server pushes newly published assets.
data_stores.source_excerpt: the web server pushes them up to the CDN's bucket

data_flows.name: serve site
data_flows.description: Reader requests and receives the public site from the web server.
data_flows.source_excerpt: readers hit the web server over HTTPS

data_flows.name: maintain content
data_flows.description: The CMS keeps pages, accounts and comments in the MySQL database.
data_flows.source_excerpt: keeps pages, accounts and comments in a MySQL database

data_flows.name: fetch assets
data_flows.description: Readers fetch images, stylesheets and downloads from the CDN.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Readers fetch those from the CDN over HTTP.

data_flows.name: publish assets
data_flows.description: The web server pushes newly published assets to the CDN bucket.
data_flows.source_excerpt: When new assets are published the web server pushes them up to the CDN's bucket.
data_flows.notes: Nothing here tells you how the push to the CDN is authenticated.

data_flows.name: maintain database
data_flows.description: The admin directly maintains the MySQL database from wherever they happen to be.
data_flows.source_excerpt: That is an unsecured MySQL connection straight to the box, no TLS on it
data_flows.notes: The source says there is no jump host and does not state the database authentication method.

trust_boundaries.name: hosted network
trust_boundaries.description: The hosted network containing the web server, CMS and MySQL database.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: The web server runs the CMS and keeps pages, accounts and comments in a MySQL database on the same hosted network.

assumptions.assumption: The web server is internet-facing because the source describes it as the public site endpoint that readers hit over HTTPS.
assumptions.basis: The source states: "Public site: readers hit the web server over HTTPS".

assumptions.assumption: The MySQL database is confidential because it contains accounts and comments, which are information about people or their activity.
assumptions.basis: The source states that the database contains "pages, accounts and comments".

assumptions.assumption: The CDN bucket contains public data because readers fetch its images, stylesheets and downloads.
assumptions.basis: The source states that readers fetch images, stylesheets and downloads from the CDN.
